en: The Philippines officially consists of 7,641 islands, not the previously taught 7,107 islands, because better mapping technology discovered 534 additional landmasses.
Mount Pulag is the highest mountain in Luzon, while Mount Apo holds the title of the highest peak in the entire Philippines.
Despite its common name, the Philippine eagle primarily hunts flying lemurs called colugos, rather than monkeys, for its main diet.
Quezon City is the largest city in the Philippines by total land area, not the historically prominent City of Manila.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines at 505 kilometers, not the shorter Pasig River located in Metro Manila.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the entire Philippines, whereas Lake Lanao is only the largest lake specifically within Mindanao.
Unlike most Philippine islands formed by volcanic activity, Palawan is geologically part of the Asian continental shelf and features limestone formations.
Taal Volcano is not a single mountain peak, but a complex system of multiple overlapping craters and lakes situated on Volcano Island.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are not volcanic cones, but rather unique geological formations of marine limestone shaped by thousands of years of rainwater erosion.
The Philippine Sea is located along the eastern coast of the archipelago facing the Pacific Ocean, not on the western side.
Before its catastrophic 1991 eruption, Mount Pinatubo was a relatively low, inconspicuous, and heavily forested mountain, not a tall and prominent peak.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were not built by Spanish colonizers, but were carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
